transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Um, well, I came in because... I've been having these eating episodes, I guess you could call them. And after they happen, I just feel so gross and disappointed in myself. I really feel like I should have more control over it. It gets bad enough that I end up writing some pretty awful things about myself in my journal. So, I figured I should probably talk to someone about it.
After these eating episodes, do you do anything to try to counteract what you've eaten, like making yourself vomit, using laxatives, exercising excessively, or restricting food afterward?

No, I don't do any of that. Um, I've never made myself throw up or taken laxatives or anything like that. And I definitely don't exercise a bunch afterward. Honestly, I usually just feel too gross and tired to do much of anything. I just kind of sit with it and feel bad about it.

When you have these eating episodes, do you feel like you're eating a much larger amount of food than most people would eat in a similar situation, and do you feel like you can't stop or control how much you're eating while it's happening?

Yeah, I do. It's definitely a lot more than normal. Like, um... on some nights after my cleaning shift, I'll stop at the convenience store just meaning to grab a regular dinner. But then I get back to my room and I end up eating a big bowl of ramen, several rice balls, fried chicken, and a bunch of sweets. I'll eat all of that within just an hour or two. And while it's happening, yeah, it really feels like I can't stop or control it at all.

Besides the eating episodes and feeling bad about yourself afterward, have you been experiencing persistent sadness, low mood, or loss of interest in things you normally enjoy over the past few weeks or months?

No, not really. Um, aside from feeling pretty terrible right after one of those eating episodes, my mood is generally okay. I'm not sad all the time, and I still like doing the things I normally enjoy. So, no, it's really just the eating stuff that's bothering me right now.
